items.title: Finite-dimensional additive Gaussian channel with average power
proof_obligations: Define finite dimension, positive-definite noise covariance, independent noise across uses, and real nats convention.
Define average block power for ordinary and feedback codes; state AC inherited from the Gaussian-law interface.

items.title: A low-error random code can be pruned to satisfy a strict average cost constraint
proof_obligations: State the random-code ensemble, per-word cost random variable, strict mean-cost gap, and expected-error hypothesis.
Use Markov bounds on the fraction of over-budget words and ensemble-average error; prove deletion preserves vanishing error and rate.

items.title: Threshold decoding bound for memoryless channels with densities
proof_obligations: Specify counting or Lebesgue reference measures, transition/output densities, support, and information density.
Prove the false-alarm likelihood-ratio expectation is one, then derive the union-bound error estimate.

items.title: Finite-simplex entropy is continuous and concave
proof_obligations: Prove continuity of -t ln t at zero and on [0,1].
Prove concavity on the closed interval, including zero coordinates, and derive 0 <= H(p) <= ln(m) including m=1.

items.title: A Gaussian maximizes scalar differential entropy at fixed variance
proof_obligations: Define differential entropy for a density with finite entropy and derive the Gaussian reference density.
Expand the KL divergence and compute the quadratic expectation to obtain the entropy bound and equality case.

items.title: Jensen's inequality for an integrable cost random variable
proof_obligations: Prove Jensen for finite concave functions on a half-line using a supporting affine function at the mean; handle the boundary mean and integrability explicitly.

items.title: A normal variable has finite fourth moment
proof_obligations: Compute the second and fourth moments by integration by parts with vanishing Gaussian boundary terms.
Scale the result to N(0,sigma^2) and state the finite-product consequence used later.

items.title: Water-filling maximizes the finite parallel Gaussian allocation objective
proof_obligations: Prove existence and uniqueness of the water level for positive total power, including inactive branches.
Prove global optimality using concavity and the active/inactive derivative inequalities; check zero power.

items.title: Zero-cost information capacity of a countable-input finite-output DMC
proof_obligations: Define countable input laws, a finite-output row-stochastic DMC, zero letter cost, finite output entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information, and the zero-cost information-capacity supremum.

items.title: Causal feedback codes for a finite-dimensional Gaussian channel
proof_obligations: Define measurable causal encoders, a decoder, uniform-message average error, and expected average power.
Define the no-feedback subcase by encoders independent of past outputs.

items.title: Orthogonal coordinates diagonalize a finite-dimensional Gaussian noise law
proof_obligations: Use the positive-definite spectral decomposition and the exact orthogonal-normal supplier to prove the transformed noise coordinates are independent with variances equal to the eigenvalues.
Prove orthogonal transformations preserve the squared-power cost and code/error correspondence; identify the AC use.

items.title: Finite-input vector Gaussian mutual information is bounded by water-filling
proof_obligations: For a finite-support input, prove all output differential entropies and KL expressions are finite.
Use orthogonal coordinates, entropy subadditivity, and the scalar Gaussian entropy bound to reduce mutual information to a power allocation problem.
Invoke the water-filling optimization lemma and show independent Gaussian inputs attain the bound.

items.title: Parallel Gaussian information density obeys a finite-variance law of large numbers
proof_obligations: Derive the output Gaussian density by completing the square, including zero-power coordinates.
Compute the information-density mean and prove its second moment is finite using the local Gaussian fourth-moment lemma.
Apply Chebyshev across independent channel uses.

items.title: Finite DMC with a nonnegative input cost and feasible budget
proof_obligations: Define a finite nonnegative cost function, its minimum and maximum, and budgets Gamma at least the minimum cost.
Define the constrained one-letter information supremum and its nats convention.

items.title: Strictly feasible Gaussian inputs yield cost-feasible Gaussian codes
proof_obligations: Use independent Gaussian inputs with total power strictly below the budget and the threshold-decoder bound.
Show the per-codeword quadratic cost concentrates using the finite fourth moment, then prune and preserve rate.

items.title: Average-cost fixed-length codes and operational DMC capacity
proof_obligations: Define the uniform-message average block cost, average-error reliable rates, and the operational supremum.
Define C_I(Gamma) as the supremum of I(P_X;W) over the feasible finite simplex; do not presume attainment.

items.title: Causal feedback codes for a finite cost-constrained DMC
proof_obligations: Define each causal encoder f_t(M,Y^{t-1}), the finite decoder, and expected average letter cost.
State that the channel law at time t depends only on the current input and is row-stochastic.

items.title: Constrained DMC information capacity is attained, nondecreasing, and concave
proof_obligations: Show the feasible simplex is nonempty and compact and the mutual-information objective is continuous, so the maximum is attained.
Prove monotonicity and concavity of C_I(Gamma).
For Gamma above minimum cost, approximate every boundary-feasible optimizer by strictly feasible input laws with convergent mutual information.

items.title: Fano's inequality for a finite message observed through a density
proof_obligations: Define the posterior probability vector from the conditional and marginal output densities and define H(M|Y).
Prove conditioning on a finite decoder output cannot lower H(M|Y) using finite KL nonnegativity, then apply Fano to that decoder output.

items.title: Strictly feasible DMC input laws achieve every lower mutual-information rate
proof_obligations: State the strict cost hypothesis and handle the zero-rate case.
Use the IID information-density limit and threshold decoder to make ensemble average error vanish.
Prove IID costs concentrate below budget and prune to a deterministic code with all retained words feasible and asymptotically unchanged rate.

items.title: An average-cost DMC block input has mutual information at most n C_I(Gamma)
proof_obligations: Use the memoryless conditional law and finite entropy chain rules to bound block mutual information by the sum of one-letter terms.
Apply concavity and monotonicity of C_I to the coordinate costs.

items.title: Capacity of finite parallel Gaussian channels with and without feedback
proof_obligations: State both ordinary and causal-feedback operational capacities under expected average power.
Prove the converse by Fano, chain rule, the conditional single-use bound, and Jensen over histories and time.
Prove achievability with the no-feedback Gaussian random code and identify the active/inactive water-filling branches and P=0 case.

items.title: Average-cost capacity formula for a finite DMC
proof_obligations: Prove the converse with finite Fano, data processing and the block mutual-information bound.
Prove achievability above minimum cost by strict-feasibility approximation; treat Gamma=min-cost separately using the restricted minimum-cost alphabet.
Check one-message and zero-capacity endpoints.

items.title: An inactive DMC cost constraint recovers ordinary capacity
proof_obligations: For Gamma at least the maximum letter cost, show every input law and every codeword satisfies the constraint.
Apply both capacity formulas with the same average-error convention and nats units.

items.title: Causal feedback does not increase finite DMC capacity under average cost
proof_obligations: Use the finite feedback Markov structure to single-letterize the message-output mutual information.
Apply the constrained one-letter information supremum conditional on each past output and Jensen across histories and times.
Show ordinary cost-feasible codes are feedback codes that ignore feedback.

title: Cost-Constrained, Gaussian, and Feedback Channels — Examples

items.title: A finite information-capacity supremum need not be attained
proof_obligations: Specify the binary rows with strictly positive crossover terms; show every input law has mutual information below ln 2; give an explicit feasible sequence tending to ln 2.

items.title: Orthogonal reduction of a correlated two-dimensional Gaussian channel
proof_obligations: Specify an orthogonal matrix and positive noise eigenvalues and compute the covariance.
Use the published orthogonal-normal theorem under AC to prove transformed noise independence.
Show the input transformation preserves the power constraint and code correspondence; evaluate the P=2 capacity example.

items.title: Water-filling for noise variances one and four
proof_obligations: Solve the water-level equation for noise variances 1 and 4 in both power regimes.
Verify the allocations are nonnegative, sum to P, and the rate formulas agree at the threshold P=3.

items.title: Cost-constrained capacity of a binary identity channel with feedback
proof_obligations: Compute the feasible binary input laws and maximize binary entropy on the constrained interval.
Check Gamma=0, Gamma=1/2 and Gamma=1, and identify the feedback capacity.
